questions.title: Set attributes on external links
questions.prompt: For every link whose `href` **starts with** `http`, set the `target` attribute to `_blank` and add the class `external`. Leave the other links alone. Use `getAttribute()` and `setAttribute()`.

setup.css:
body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }
a.external::after { content: " ↗"; }

hints: link.getAttribute("href") returns the attribute exactly as written.

tests.name: External links open in a new tab and have the class
tests.code:
const ext = [...document.querySelectorAll("a")].filter(a => a.getAttribute("href").startsWith("http"));
return ext.length === 2 && ext.every(a => a.getAttribute("target") === "_blank" && a.classList.contains("external"));

tests.name: Local links are unchanged
Uses setAttribute()

questions.title: Form methods and events
questions.prompt:
1. When the page loads, move the focus to the `#username` field.
2. When the **Clear** button is clicked, call the form's `reset()` method and put the focus back in `#username`.
3. When `#username` loses focus (`blur` event), convert its value to lowercase.

setup.html:
<form id="signup">
  <label>Username: <input type="text" id="username"></label>
  <label>City: <input type="text" id="city" value="Fresno"></label>
  <button type="button" id="clear">Clear</button>
</form>
setup.css: body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }

tests.name: Calls focus() when the page loads
Blur lowercases the username
Clear resets the form and focuses username

questions.title: Register: list the errors
questions.prompt:
Like the chapter's Register application: when **Register** is clicked, check the fields and show each problem as an `<li>` in `#errors` (clear old errors first):

- `Email is required.` if the email is blank
- `Password must be at least 8 characters.`
- `You must accept the terms.` if the box isn't checked

If there are no errors, show `Registered!` in `#status`; otherwise make `#status` empty.

setup.css:
body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }
#errors { color: #c0392b; }

hints: Collect messages in an array, then create one li per message.
Clear the list with errorsList.innerHTML = "" (or remove its children).

tests.name: Empty form shows all three errors
tests.code:
document.getElementById("register").click();
return [...document.querySelectorAll("#errors li")].map(l => l.textContent).join("|") === "Email is required.|Password must be at least 8 characters.|You must accept the terms.";

tests.name: Errors are cleared before showing new ones
A valid form shows "Registered!" and no errors

questions.title: innerHTML versus textContent
questions.prompt:
The user's comment in the starter code contains HTML. Show it in two places:

- In `#safe`, show it as **plain text** (the tags appear as typed), using `textContent`.
- In `#list`, use `innerHTML` to build a `<ul>` with one `<li>` per tag word in `tags` (these are trusted).

Then store in `safeHasBold` whether `#safe` contains a `<b>` element (it shouldn't).

setup.css: body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }

hints: textContent never parses HTML; innerHTML does.
Build the HTML string with a loop or tags.map(...).join("").

tests.name: #safe shows the tags as text
#list has a ul with 3 li items
safeHasBold is false
